title: iTutorGroup age-based application screening
system_purpose: Filter applications for remote English tutoring roles
decision_impact: The configured software could prevent an applicant from reaching human hiring consideration
affected_groups: older applicants; women applicants; men applicants
verified_facts: The EEOC reported that iTutorGroup's online application software was alleged to automatically reject female applicants aged 55 or older and male applicants aged 60 or older.
reported_harm: The reported automatic screening created alleged opportunity loss and age discrimination for applicants who were prevented from advancing.
quantitative_evidence: The EEOC reported more than 200 older applicants and a $365000 settlement; the source does not provide a selection-rate denominator.
limitations: The source reports allegations resolved through settlement and does not provide a technical audit; the automation may have been a configured rule rather than a machine-learning model.

title: Amazon experimental resume-screening tool
system_purpose: Rank resumes to identify candidates for recruiter attention
decision_impact: The score could influence which applicants received recruiter attention and therefore access to interviews
affected_groups: women applicants; applicants with gender-correlated resume signals; recruiters
verified_facts: EEOC-hosted testimony recounts reporting that Amazon began developing a resume-screening tool in 2014 and scrapped it after identifying bias against female applicants in its experimental system.
reported_harm: The reported training-data and feature effects could create discriminatory opportunity loss by lowering the ranking of women or resumes containing gender-correlated signals.
quantitative_evidence: The testimony gives the 2014 development and 2018 reporting timeline but no affected-applicant count, deployment rate or validated selection-rate gap.
limitations: This is a reported experimental tool rather than a regulator finding about a production decision; the testimony is not an adjudicative finding and does not independently verify the technical mechanism.
